questions.q: Why was Captain Smollett angry right after Silver left?
choices: Everyone except Gray had left their posts
Silver had stolen the chart from the doctor
Jim had run off into the woods yet again
Someone had fired a shot at Silver's back as he left
questions.evidence: found not a man of us at his post but Gray

questions.q: Why did the captain say he had spoken so harshly ("red-hot") to Silver?
choices: He did it on purpose, knowing it would bring an attack
He lost his temper by accident and was sorry for it
He wanted to shame Silver in front of his own men
He hoped harsh words would make Silver give up the ship
questions.evidence: I pitched it in red-hot on purpose

questions.q: How were the loaded muskets arranged for the defenders?
choices: On four piles of firewood, one near the middle of each side
Hanging from pegs on the walls on either side of the door
Locked in the doctor's chest in the centre of the house
Buried in the sand outside, ready to be dug up quickly
questions.evidence: the firewood had been built into four piles

questions.q: Why did the captain order the fire to be tossed out?
choices: So smoke would not get in their eyes during the fight
To save the firewood for cooking the next day's dinner
Because sparks might set the log-house roof on fire
So the gunners on the ship could not aim at the light
questions.evidence: we mustn't have smoke in our eyes

questions.q: Why did the captain put the squire and Gray on the long north side?
choices: It had five loopholes and was where the danger was
It was the coolest and shadiest side of the house
It faced the anchorage where the ship was lying
It had the best view down the hill to the sea

questions.q: What job did the captain give Jim during the attack?
choices: To help load the muskets
To guard the door with a pistol
To fire from the long north side
To run to the woods for Ben Gunn
questions.evidence: we'll stand by to load and bear a hand

questions.q: What started the shooting after the long, hot wait?
choices: Joyce fired his musket
A cannonball struck the roof
Silver blew a shrill whistle
Anderson shouted a war cry
questions.evidence: suddenly Joyce whipped up his musket and fired

questions.q: Why did the defenders decide the real attack would come from the north?
choices: Most of the first shots came from the north side
The north side was the only wall without loopholes
The doctor had seen Silver hiding to the north
The wind was blowing their smoke toward the north
questions.evidence: It was plain, therefore, that the attack would be developed from the north

questions.q: What happened to Hunter when a pirate reached his loophole?
choices: A pirate yanked away his musket and knocked him senseless
He was shot through the head and fell dead at his post
He threw open the door and ran out into the stockade
He was dragged out over the fence and taken prisoner
questions.evidence: laid the poor fellow senseless on the floor

questions.q: "Our position was utterly reversed." Here "reversed" means:
choices: Turned the opposite way
Made much stronger and safer
Kept exactly the same as before
Hidden from the enemy's sight

questions.q: What happened when Jim came face to face with Anderson?
choices: Jim leaped aside, slipped in the soft sand, and rolled down
Jim swung his cutlass and cut Anderson down at the door
Anderson grabbed Jim by the collar and took him prisoner
Jim turned and ran back inside the house to the captain
questions.evidence: missing my foot in the soft sand, rolled headlong down the slope

questions.q: Who cut down Job Anderson, the big boatswain?
choices: Gray
Jim
The doctor
The squire
questions.evidence: Gray, following close behind me, had cut down the big boatswain

questions.q: What price did the loyal party pay for the victory?
choices: Joyce was killed, Hunter was stunned, and the captain was hurt
The squire and the doctor were both shot dead at the loopholes
They lost the stockade and the pirates pulled down their flag
Gray was carried off as a prisoner by the fleeing pirates
questions.evidence: Joyce by his, shot through the head, never to move again

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The pirates attack the stockade and are beaten off, but at a cost
The loyal party slips away at night and sails off on the HISPANIOLA
Silver and the captain shake hands and agree to share the treasure
Jim sneaks out of the stockade alone to look for Ben Gunn's boat
questions.evidence: the fight was over and the victory was ours
